newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares finished strongly up on Monday, bouyed by a better bullion price, but some profit-taking before the close of trade dragged major indices off their day highs.

Dealers said some futures play was seen on the buy side in the morning and this further boosted industrial shares, but overall market volumes were thin. Stronger European markets also boosted the mood of local shares.
"The market was pushed firmer on the bullion price. It has been a big sentiment driver for the whole market," Investec international dealer Dominic Rey told Reuters.

One of the features of the day was the thin volumes traded in gold shares which dealers said indicated that players were a little sceptical of a follow-through from the bullion price. Overall volumes traded were 720 million rand worth of stocks.
However, most gold shares showed strong gains.
Western Areas jumped 8.62 percent to 31.50 rand, Western Deep gained 5.34 percent to 108.50 rand and Kloof was up 3.45 percent to 27 rand.
Dealers said trade on Tuesday would be determined by the direction of the bullion price which has been dominating the market.
The gold index finished up 34.8 points to 999.6 points, the industrial index climbed 34.8 points to a record closing high of 8842.5 points and the all-share index added 32.6 points to 7,380.6 points.

A bookover of 800,000 shares and a foreign purchase deal pushed computer firm Persetel higher on Monday, making it one of the biggest movers on the Johannesburg bourse. It ended up 20 cents to 33.10 rand.
Primedia recovered from recent lows which were prompted by market views that the media firm was set to pay a big premium for a stake in cinema group Interleisure.
Primedia ended up 160 cents to 30 rand and Interleisure was up 20 cents to 820 cents.
MGX rose 35 cents to 19.35 rand after the firm announced it had made two acquisitions which could prop up its targeted year-end earnings, dealers said.

Near-dated industrial share futures opened strong in quiet trade but soon met resistance at the 8,600 level where arbitrage opportunities with the cash market were opened. They came off highs in the afternoon as the cash market was pressured, dealers said.

Gold contracts remained strong after rallying to a high of 713 but profit-taking at those levels eroded some gains by the end of the trading session. Bullion's grip on firmer levels was still a positive factor and dealers said golds would test higher levels on Tuesday depending on the stability of the gold price.
The September all-share contract was last at 6,710/22 from 6,685, the industrial contract was at 8,560/68 from 8,530 and the gold contract was at 690/704 from 674.
